title: Protocol for the Collection and Quantitative Processing of Archaeological Sediment Samples
author: Jesús Bermejo Tirado

steps.title: Select Stratigraphic Units (UE)
steps.instruction: Identify stratigraphic units (UUEE) associated with use or circulation levels. Exclude abandonment, filling, leveling, or foundation levels to avoid 'Pompeii Premise' inferential problems.

steps.title: Establish Sampling Grids
steps.instruction: Set up two parallel sampling types for each selected deposit before complete excavation.

substeps.instruction: Regular Sampling: Establish a grid of 50 cm² modules across the area. For partial levels or very small sectors, the density may be reduced to 10 x 10 cm grids.
Random Sampling (Control): Use the regular grid as a reference to distribute random samples proportionally across the deposit area.

steps.title: Prepare Sample Containers
steps.instruction: Prepare plastic zip-lock bags (e.g., 2-liter capacity) and label them with an indelible marker using the following uppercase code: SITE NAME - CAMPAIGN - SECTOR - UE - SAMPLING TYPE - CORRELATIVE NUMBER (e.g., Closos - 2025 - Naveta 1 - UE 234 - Muestreo Regular - 1).

substeps.instruction: Use different number ranges for regular and random sampling to avoid confusion.

steps.title: Collect Sediment Samples
steps.instruction: Collect sediment samples using disposable latex gloves. Stop excavation during sampling to avoid stratigraphic contamination; all samples from a level must be collected at once.

substeps.instruction: Use a consistent container with volume markings (e.g., a plastic pitcher or clean cut tetra-brik) and clean it with a cloth between samples.
Collect 1 liter of sediment per sample, ideally from a depth of 6 to 10 cm from the upper level quota.
For regular sampling, extract from the center of the grid square.
For well-defined pavements/floors, ensure samples are taken above the pavement surface.

If 1 liter is unavailable: prioritize the regular sample over the random sample. If less than 1 liter is available in a grid, collect the maximum amount possible (even 4 cm³ may suffice for some organic analyses).

steps.title: Label and Document Samples
steps.instruction: Place the sediment in the labeled bag and insert an acetate sheet labeled with the same code used for the bag.

steps.title: Georeference Extraction Points
steps.instruction: Georeference the center of each extraction point using a total station or sub-centimetric GPS.

substeps.instruction: Assign each point a code without spaces: SITE INITIALS_CAMPAIGN_SECTOR INITIALS_UE_TYPE INITIALS_CORRELATIVE NUMBER (e.g., CLOS_2025_NAV1_UE234_REG_1 or CLOS_2025_NAV1_UE234_ALE_56).
Ensure the point code matches the bag label code, especially the correlative number.

steps.title: Maintain Sampling Log
steps.instruction: Create a sampling diary to record all technical data and sample lists.

substeps.instruction: Note coordinate systems, software, and reference device models used.
Include a sketch of each sampling operation per deposit.
List all samples collected daily using the established nomenclature.
Record the georeference point codes in the diary.
Take a photo of the sample lists at the end of each day.
Download georeferenced points daily and verify them via GIS before continuing UE excavation.

steps.title: Store and Transport Samples
steps.instruction: Store samples in cardboard boxes, filling them to maximum capacity to prevent bags from moving and breaking, without over-pressurizing them.

substeps.instruction: Attach a visible list to each box detailing the stored samples using the established code (e.g., Closos - 2025 - Naveta 1 - UE 234 - Muestreo Regular - 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8).
Store boxes in an area avoiding humidity and abrupt temperature changes.
